rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this tiny 9-function program (1781 text bytes) has ample headroom to shift from a conservative profile toward maximum resistance: all seven passes stay enabled with SecurityGain/DiversityGain raised across the board to push per-function selection toward applying more transforms. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain (0.9) since control-flow flattening is the strongest structural defense for the branch-heavy cores (QuickSort, BubbleSort, main's dispatch), with a moderate RuntimeCost weight (0.6) acknowledging its loop-overhead so hot sorting loops aren't over-penalized by stacking every costly transform. BCF follows at 0.8 SecurityGain with low SizeCost (0.2) because the binary is so small that its code-size explosion is essentially free here, while its RuntimeCost (0.5) stays elevated since bogus arithmetic sits inside the comparison loops. SPLIT and IBR carry the highest DiversityGain (0.8) because they add structural variety cheaply and compose well with FLA/BCF without redundant overlap. ICALL and IGV remain enabled at moderate risk weights (0.3/0.2) — indirect calls and global-variable hiding add useful indirection layers on this pointer-heavy list-manipulation code (ReadList, PrintList) at low correctness risk, as confirmed by the clean round-1 run. SUB stays the lowest-cost baseline (RuntimeCost 0.2) since instruction substitution is nearly free and should apply broadly even to the tightest loops.
